mission_title: Editorial AI Course Studio + Human Approval Publisher
objective: Build an authenticated editorial workflow in XPeX Academy where authorized staff can Generate with AI -> Review -> Edit -> Approve -> Publish into native LearnHouse Course/Chapter/Activity services. Human approval and a separate explicit publish action are mandatory. LearnHouse remains the source of truth after publication.
principles: No AI provider secret in client code
OPENROUTER_API_KEY and HF_TOKEN remain server-side only
Reuse LearnHouse native auth, role, Course, Chapter and Activity services
Do not create a second LMS or parallel enrollment/progress system
Fail closed on provider, validation, permission, approval or persistence errors
Do not fabricate certifications, partners, enrollments, metrics, testimonials or claims
All approval/publish writes must be auditable and tied to an authenticated actor

allowed: REVIEWED -> APPROVED only without unresolved BLOCKER
APPROVED -> DRAFT when approved content is edited
APPROVED -> PUBLISHED only by explicit authorized publish action

backend_scope: Create authenticated editorial endpoints/services for generate, retrieve, edit, review, approve and publish
Preserve provider provenance, timestamps, actor UUID, topic, audience, module count and schema version
Persist approval metadata before publication if durable workflow requires it
Map validated APPROVED CourseDraft into native LearnHouse Course/Chapter/Activity services
Make publication idempotent or safely reject duplicates
Reject publish unless status is APPROVED and no unresolved BLOCKER exists
Never mutate learner enrollment, progress, completion or certification during editorial publication
Return native authoritative identifiers after publish
frontend_scope: Add authenticated staff/editorial Course Studio screen using existing XPeX/LearnHouse UI conventions
Actions: Gerar com IA -> Revisar -> Aprovar -> Publicar
Show provider provenance, review notes and severity
Disable/hide protected actions for unauthorized users
Publish must remain a separate deliberate action after approval
After publish, link to native LearnHouse destination using authoritative IDs
authorization: Discover and reuse existing LearnHouse/XPeX role and permission primitives
Do not invent a separate auth system
Enforce approval and publication authorization server-side
At minimum restrict editorial actions to authenticated authorized staff
security: Treat generated/stored draft text as untrusted data
Do not log provider tokens or Authorization headers
Validate AI output with Pydantic before persistence/publication
Avoid client-controlled approval/publication status mass assignment

publisher_contract.output: native LearnHouse course/chapter/activity identifiers and canonical navigation target

backend: duplicate publish idempotent or safely rejected
provider failures fail closed without secret leakage
prompt injection content remains data only
regression: migration dry-run passes if schema changes exist

live_validation.environment: Railway production after merge and successful deploy

steps: verify native LearnHouse records and authoritative identifiers

observability: Log state transitions with draft identifier and actor UUID without secrets
Log provider/model and sanitized result status
Log publish attempt/success/failure with native LearnHouse identifiers
documentation: Update docs/xpex/launch/XPEX_CONTENT_STUDIO.md or create linked CONTENT-002 runbook
Document state machine, permissions, publish contract, rollback and smoke procedure
Document that provider secrets belong only in Railway server variables

Evidence confirms no automatic publish before explicit Publish action
